blocks.text: Isaiah’s unusual public action belongs to a setting in which reliance on foreign coalitions and military resources is challenged. The chapter presents Egypt and Ethiopia as the hoped-for help, then depicts their humiliation and captivity under Assyria; the final question exposes the resulting fear: if those relied upon cannot stand, where can escape be found? This can be read as making trust in YHWH a political as well as religious issue. Isaiah’s action also fits the book’s varied portrayal of him through speeches, reports, sign actions, and royal narratives.
